- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 35.94, 36.62) — fails to anticipate or overreact to them.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly pulls prices back toward historical averages after spikes.
- Forecast horizon (30d) shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum — especially after a spike, model delays recognition of continuation.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” behavior after price spikes — forecasts peak higher than true outcome, then drop too fast.
- Model underestimates volatility in late periods — fails to capture sharp reversals or sudden spikes near end of forecast window.
- Model tends to smooth out noise — underweights short-term volatility, leading to overly stable-looking forecasts.
- Forecast bias is upward — consistently predicts higher prices than true outcome, especially in mid-to-late forecast window.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shifts — e.g., regulatory changes or auction timing not reflected in forecast.
